nodes.label: CSS Specificity
nodes.rationale: Higher-order digit always wins; ties go to later rule; keep specificity low so styles are easy to override

nodes.label: !important
nodes.rationale: Last resort: breaks debugging, causes cascading !important wars, hurts readability

nodes.label: External Stylesheet
nodes.rationale: Recommended for separation of concerns and browser caching

nodes.label: rem vs em Units
nodes.rationale: em compounds when nested; rem is predictable and scales with user font settings

nodes.label: box-sizing: border-box
nodes.rationale: Makes width include padding and border, simplifying layout math

nodes.label: CSS position and z-index
nodes.rationale: Common pattern: relative parent, absolute child

nodes.label: CSS Inheritance
nodes.rationale: Text properties inherit, box/layout properties do not

nodes.label: Flexbox
nodes.rationale: 1D layout for aligning items inside components

nodes.label: CSS Grid
nodes.rationale: 2D layout for whole-page structure; repeat(auto-fill, minmax()) gives responsive without media queries

nodes.label: Transform, Transition, Animation
nodes.rationale: transform moves visually without affecting flow and performs better than top/left

nodes.label: Mobile First
nodes.rationale: Forces choosing essential content first and simplifies cascade with min-width additions

nodes.label: CSS Custom Properties
nodes.rationale: Live at runtime and changeable from JS (e.g. dark mode), unlike SCSS variables

nodes.label: SCSS Preprocessor
nodes.rationale: Variables, nesting, mixins, modules; transpiled to CSS by build tools

nodes.label: var, let, const
nodes.rationale: Use const by default, let when reassigning, never var (function scope and silent redeclare)

nodes.label: Hoisting
nodes.rationale: TDZ ReferenceError for let/const is safer than silent undefined

nodes.label: Primitive vs Object Types
nodes.rationale: Primitives copy values; objects copy references, governing copying and argument passing

nodes.label: Strict Equality (===)
nodes.rationale: == implicit coercion is unpredictable

nodes.label: Function Declarations, Expressions, Arrow Functions
nodes.rationale: Arrow functions use lexical this, preferred for callbacks

nodes.label: Call by Value vs Call by Sharing
this Binding
nodes.rationale: Determined by call site, not declaration

nodes.label: Constructor Functions and prototype
nodes.rationale: Methods on prototype are shared across instances for memory efficiency; class syntax builds on this

nodes.label: DOM (Document Object Model)
nodes.rationale: DOM is the browser's parsed result, not the HTML file

nodes.label: classList style toggling
nodes.rationale: Keeps style definitions in CSS, JS only toggles state (separation of concerns)

nodes.label: XSS via innerHTML
nodes.rationale: Use textContent for text to avoid XSS

nodes.label: addEventListener
nodes.rationale: Multiple handlers, bubbling/capture control, removable, separation of concerns

nodes.label: Event Delegation
nodes.rationale: One handler on parent saves memory and handles dynamically added children

nodes.label: Event Loop
nodes.rationale: Single-threaded JS stays responsive by deferring async continuations

nodes.label: Microtask Queue vs Task Queue
nodes.rationale: Microtasks drain before tasks, so Promise.then runs before setTimeout(0)

nodes.label: Timer API (setTimeout, setInterval)
nodes.rationale: Timers are provided by browser, not engine; clear intervals in SPAs

nodes.label: Storage API (localStorage, sessionStorage)
nodes.rationale: Values always strings; use JSON for objects

nodes.label: fetch API
nodes.rationale: Rejects only on network failure; check response.ok

nodes.label: ES Modules
nodes.rationale: Module scope isolation avoids global variable collisions; requires local server (not file://)
